target_customer: TypeScript developers and engineering teams that need reliable long-running background jobs and AI agent workflows
problem: Serverless platforms time out on long tasks, so developers hand-build queues, retries and observability for background work.
business_model: Open source core with usage-based managed cloud and self-hosting option
product_category: Developer tools, background jobs and durable workflow platform

founders.name: Matt Aitken
founders.background_notes: YC page says he created two iPad apps that won Apple's iPad App of the Year.

founders.name: Eric Allam
founders.background_notes: YC page says he was CTO of Code School.

founders.name: Dan Patel
founders.background_notes: No further background on the YC page.

founders.name: James Ritchie
founders.background_notes: YC page says he was a product lead at several VC-backed startups.

technical_complexity.rationale: Durable execution, queues, retries, observability and elastic infrastructure are hard for a small team, and later versions needed custom runtimes.

defensibility.rationale: Open source code can be copied or self-hosted; lock-in comes from SDK integration and run history, and the YC page and site show customers such as Cal.com and Supabase.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquired or shut it down through 2026; it raised a Series A in December 2025.

market_need_then: Developers on serverless stacks such as Vercel lacked long-running job support, and the company reported early open source traction of over 4,000 GitHub stars by August 2023.

branding.domain_note: Uses the .dev domain trigger.dev; acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: Own logo not described by the sources found
identity.visual_style: A third-party design analysis describes a near-black site with a lime accent
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, developer-focused short headlines such as No timeouts

branding.community_and_virality: Open source community on GitHub and Discord per the seed post; Hacker News launches. No merch or fan accounts found.

brand_strength.rationale: Well known in TypeScript developer circles through open source and Hacker News, but the name is descriptive and no brand-specific press was found.

outcome_analysis: Trigger.dev grew from an open source Zapier-style tool into a background jobs framework and then an AI agent workflow platform. It raised a 3 million dollar seed in August 2023 on open source traction, then a 16 million dollar Series A in December 2025 led by Standard Capital. Reliability incidents in late 2025 and June 2026 are a risk, but the sources found show no layoffs or exit.
notes: Series A date is the blog post date 2025-12-17; aggregators differ on the lead (one says Bryan Berg, the company blog says Standard Capital). No dated 2022 or 2023 competitor source was found in the competitor search (results were 2026 comparison pages and an undated Hacker News mirror), so the list is empty; Temporal and Inngest are later-described alternatives. The YC page lists no education for founders.
